marta_cs: FYI a customer just pinged asking why the 'confidence' numbers from our ranking endpoint are negative and not between 0-1. Client thinks it's a bug. :thinking:

samir_ml: quick note — those are unnormalized logits from the model, not probabilities. negative values are expected. we don't post-process to save cycles. :fyi:

elena_eng: adding some quick repro steps we asked the customer for. can we confirm a minimal curl example?

marta_cs: here's what they sent (sanitized):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ranking
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
{
  "model": "redwood-rank-v1",
  "inputs": "Which movie should i watch tonight?",
  "candidates": ["Inception","The Matrix","Some Indie Film"],
  "top_k": 3
}
```
Response they got: 
```
{
  "candidates": ["Inception","The Matrix","Some Indie Film"],
  "scores": [-1.75, 0.27, -0.43]
}
```

marta_cs: they expected [0..1] probs and were surprised negatives showed up and that values don't sum to 1.

samir_ml: short expl for CS: those numbers are model logits (raw affinity). To get probabilities do softmax over the vector: p_i = exp(s_i) / sum_j exp(s_j). Negative logits are normal and just reflect lower raw preference.

samir_ml: example conversion (python):
```
import math
scores = [-1.75, 0.27, -0.43]
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e/sum(exp) for e in exp]
# probs ~ [0.059, 0.696, 0.245]
```

elena_eng: for telemetry reasons we return raw scores (cheaper, smaller payload). If clients want probs, we should add a documented snippet or a small query param. filing a docs note after this thread.

marta_cs: customer asks: is there any chance these are 'scores' that depend on candidate ordering or padding? they saw different numbers when they shuffled candidates.

samir_ml: good catch — ordering should NOT matter for a proper reranker, but some optimizations (batching + prefix caching) can produce slight numeric differences if tokenization/prefixes change. we should ask them to provide exact requests (including candidate order) and a deterministic single-call curl so we can reproduce.

elena_eng: diagnostic checklist for CS to request from customer: 1) full curl + headers (including model name + version) 2) exact candidates array order 3) whether they observed differences across multiple calls 4) tokenization trim rules (if they pre-tokenize) 5) sample raw response body (we already have an example)

marta_cs: i've asked them for that. i also told them how to normalize on their side with softmax and that negatives are expected. they want a one-line explanation to share with their PM.

samir_ml: one-liner you can give them: "The ranking endpoint returns raw model preference scores (logits) which can be negative; to interpret them as probabilities apply a softmax over the score vector — we return logits by default for performance and reproducibility."

elena_eng: action items: @samir_ml to confirm whether we ever changed behavior to return probs (I think no). @marta_cs to collect repro data. I'll open a small docs PR with the python/curl examples and mention numeric non-determinism edge cases.

alert-bot: Note: created ticket CS-1129 -> "Clarify ranking output semantics + docs examples" assigned to docs-team.

marta_cs: thanks all. i'll update the customer and paste the follow-up here once they send the curl. :thumbsup:
